narrative: Round 26 targeted only bp35 L9. A fresh 342-action replay first reached levels_completed=8, GameState.NOT_FINISHED, settled sha256 375b7eddf99ae0a2ef41439fe15d92d2c8925b57720f3c6c833b9bb64711d2c0. The round-25 survivor paths were rechecked, then the survival/death crack was isolated with matched controls: at x26.5/+2.5 and camera -26, the same click(3,5) under the same gravity lands alive at x26.5/-9.5 in 22 layers when door 3 is closed, but runs 47 layers to GAME_OVER when that support is pre-opened. Trigger category is therefore not the discriminator; a reachable support in the flight column is. That model exposed the missing construction order. From x32/+2.5, door 3 is opened remotely before entering its column, an otherwise-unused x27 body is built, and repeated body carries produce alive rests at -15.5, -21.5, -27.5, -33.5, -39.5, and -45.5, directly entering the former dead zone. A side-channel shuttle then reaches x56.5/-75.5. Public frames there reveal the eight color-12 blocks at world rows -83..-79 and, above them, sparse landing structures. Opening the unsupported x15 block dies, while opening x27 lands under a door at -87.5 and opening x45 survives a 42-row ascent to a pillar at -117.5. One carry reaches -123.5; a lateral body bridge reaches x15, where a newly live color-14 door at x7..11 opens a passage through the formerly solid cols6..12 divider. Two LEFT actions put the player alive in the cols0..5 shaft at x3.5/-129.5. That view exposes a nine-switch color-8 bank at screen y3. The fixed suffix click(9,3), click(3,35), click(15,3), click(3,35), click(21,3), click(3,35), click(27,3), click(3,35), click(33,3), RIGHT, RIGHT reaches GameState.WIN and levels_completed=9 on full action 410. The official reproduction gate and five independent fresh replays all passed. bp35 is now reproducibly complete at 9/9.
novel_mechanics_found: Flight outcome is support-topology-dependent rather than switch-trigger-dependent. In the strongest matched pair, the same switch click from the same x26.5/+2.5 rest lands alive in 22 layers over a closed door but dies in 47 layers over the pre-opened door column.

Remote-open-before-entry is the missing door-column ascent primitive: open door 3 while the player is still at x32, build the unused x27 body, move onto it, and ride it upward. This yields the first live rests throughout the old [-48,-13] dead zone.

The color-12 ceiling is a column selector. Removing a block launches immediately under UP gravity; x15 has no upper support and dies in 48 layers, x27 lands under a door at world -87.5 in 17 layers, and x45 leaves the viewport for one layer but is camera-reacquired under a pillar at world -117.5 after 45 layers.
The upper x7..11 color-14 door is horizontal: from x15.5/-123.5 it can be opened safely, and two LEFT moves traverse the historical cols6..12 divider into the x3 shaft.

The live shaft-top view contains nine full 21-cell color-8 switches at screen centers (9,3), (15,3), (21,3), (27,3), (33,3), (39,3), (45,3), (51,3), and (57,3). Alternating the first five with the shaft switch at (3,35), then moving RIGHT twice, is the terminal routing sequence.

Camera pan/reacquisition is a consequence of a valid remote landing. The winning route includes supported ascents of 12, 42, and larger camera-spanning distances; unsupported open columns still terminate after the sprite leaves the frame.
bounded_negative_results: A 35-point fresh-environment sweep across the first door footprint (screen x13..17, y20..26) found only the complete 32-cell carve for y20..25 and inert clicks at y26; no partial door carve or shelf was available.

All 256 subsets of the eight accessible color-12 toggles at the first upper rest produced the same bounded death signature on the next unsupported x27 carry: GAME_OVER at level 8, 18 layers, final inferred camera -90, and no player sprite. Toggle combinations alone do not cap that column.

Matched movement entries into every pre-opened lower door column died from both tested sides. Closing the corresponding door supplied the landing and survived, so horizontal entry does not make an open door safe.
At x15.5/-75.5, clicking the x15 color-12 block immediately produced a 48-layer GAME_OVER with player absent in layers 20..48; there is no hidden support above that column.
At x27.5/-87.5, opening the supporting upper door produced a 47-layer GAME_OVER; the door is a valid landing only while closed.

At x45.5/-117.5, one pillar carry reaches -123.5 alive in 12 layers, while a second direct carry crushes against the next native row in 18 layers. The winning continuation is a lateral bridge, not a second carry.

Repeated clicks on the initial pillar after its first growth were inert, remote builds before a seed existed were inert, and the 45-point early body sweep exposed no off-center alignment. These controls ruled out an easier direct high-column construction.
next_leads: Use the exact 410-label derivation and checksum in this artifact as the bp35 9/9 reproduction authority; no further level-discovery work remains for this game.

If sequence optimization is useful, shorten only after preserving the official 410-action replay as a control. The largest likely redundancies are construction clicks before the x45 upper ascent, not the final eleven-action switch/RIGHT suffix.

Generalize the support-topology rule to future gravity games: classify the first actual solid object in the flight column from public frames instead of treating viewport exit, trigger type, or gravity direction as the death predicate.
